title: Priest (1993) rigid block, reference geometry (60° face)

meta.title: Priest (1993) rigid block, reference geometry (60° face)
meta.notes: Priest's example 8.1 with his geometry: a 60° face 30 m high (crest at x = 17.321), a 30° plane from the toe, a vertical 15 m tension crack 8.66 m behind the crest holding 3.75 m of water, and a water table rising from the toe to 3.75 m above the plane at the crack.

source.reference: Priest, S.D. (1993). Discontinuity Analysis for Rock Engineering. Chapman & Hall, London; example 8.1, pp. 224–225.
source.derived_from: cSlope verification problem V080 (MIT License), https://github.com/ZilanCiftci/cslope
notes: Crest at (17.321, 30) as in Priest's fig. 8.2 and solution (his corners A (0, 0), B (17.32, 30), C (25.98, 30), D (25.98, 15); G = 8119 kN, U = 551 kN, V = 68.9 kN; γw = 9.8 in his solution, 9.807 here, 0.0001 on F) and in commercial program B's Fig. 106; V079 is the other programs' version with the crest at 17.0. commercial program B Janbu 1.049.
cSlope fija options.tolerance = 0.001 (tolerancia del solver) en sus checks; no se importa: ogs usa analysis.tolerance = 1e-05.
grieta de tracción: profundidad 15 m, fracción de agua 0.25 (cSlope tensionCrackDepth y tensionCrackWater); en ogs es `analysis.tension_crack {depth, water_fill}` (F5.2).
